text:
All fixed. The issue was that the "bottom row" and "left column" loops ran unconditionally, so when the remaining sub-matrix collapsed to a single row or single column, those loops re-emitted elements already collected. Adding `if top != bottom` and `if left != right` guards fixes it:

- `spiral([[1, 2, 3]])` → `[1, 2, 3]` ✓
- 3×4 matrix → exactly 12 values in correct spiral order ✓
- Single column, single element, empty matrix, and square matrices all still correct; input not modified; all existing tests pass.

arguments.summary: Fixed the spiral-order bug in grid/spiral.py: the bottom-row and left-column loops ran unconditionally, so when the remaining sub-matrix was a single row (top == bottom) or single column (left == right), elements were emitted twice. Added `if top != bottom` and `if left != right` guards around those...
